sections.skill: Recognize made-up answers and verify facts that matter

questions.prompt: What is a hallucination in AI output?

choices.text: A picture the tool draws of someone's dream
A confident answer that is wrong or invented

questions.correct_answer: A confident answer that is wrong or invented
questions.intro: AI tools can produce answers that sound confident but are wrong or invented, sometimes called HALLUCINATIONS: a fake statistic, a law that does not exist, a made-up source, or a wrong price. sections.skill: A confident friend who sometimes guesses

questions.domain: Foundation 12: AI as a practical helper
questions.prompt: Is a confident tone proof that an answer is right?
questions.correct_answer: No
questions.intro: Some people answer every question confidently, even when they are guessing: "Oh yes, the store closes at 9." Sometimes they are right, sometimes not. You would check the store's own hours before driving there. AI tools can be like that friend. A confident tone is not proof; checking the original source is. That one extra step can save a wasted trip.
